clue.text: A deficiency said to terrify London's hub of finance

indicators.note: said signals that the clue words are to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: terrify means scare, and the City is London's financial district, so scare-City spoken aloud

explanation.surface: Someone warns of a shortfall that would frighten the Square Mile's bankers.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARE + CITY spoken aloud sounds like the answer; the City is the square mile of London that houses its banks and markets.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage or lack of something is the state of it being scarce.

clue.text: Discouraged detective went wrong

parts.note: erred means made a mistake, went wrong

explanation.surface: A police officer lost heart after bungling the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deterred has been put off or dissuaded from acting.

clue.text: On second thoughts change the book for the services

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is what a letter-writer adds as an afterthought after signing off
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A vicar reconsiders and swaps the book used at church services.
explanation.walkthrough: PS, the postscript added at a letter's end, stands for an afterthought; 'services' are church services, not the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is a volume of the Psalms used in church worship.

clue.text: A Borneo state -initially badly run -that is overthrown

indicators.note: initially picks out only the opening letter of the word badly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: overthrown turns the abbreviation upside down, which in a down clue reads it bottom to top

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Bornean sultanate, poorly governed, sees its rulers toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' turns IE into EI at the foot of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on the north coast of the island of Borneo.

clue.text: Sportsman in the Highlands

parts.note: describes the Scottish attendant who guides anglers and deer-stalkers on a Highland estate

explanation.walkthrough: A gillie is the Scottish attendant who looks after people fishing or shooting; strictly he serves the sportsman rather than being one, so the clue is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland ghillie is a hunting or fishing guide employed on a Scottish estate.

clue.text: I'm returning with five special agents

definitions.text: I'm returning with five special agents

parts.words: I'm returning with five special agents
parts.note: I'M read backwards gives MI, and five gives 5: MI5, Britain's domestic intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A spy chief comes back bringing five operatives.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds not the answer's letters but its example: MI5, the British security agency, named for the 'I'm' turned round plus the number five.
explanation.definitionFit: A government intelligence organisation employs agents working undercover on special missions.

clue.text: Ticklish feeling on the 2.555th day of bondage

definitions.text: Ticklish feeling on the 2.555th day of bondage

parts.words: Ticklish feeling on the 2.555th day of bondage
parts.note: 2,555 days is seven times 365, and the bondage is marriage, so this is the restlessness said to strike a married couple at that point

explanation.walkthrough: The 'bondage' is wedlock; the phrase is the folk idea that spouses grow restless after that many years, made famous by a 1955 Marilyn Monroe film.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the urge to stray said to afflict people some years into a marriage.

clue.text: The quality having influence

parts.note: describes the property of producing a result or making an impact

explanation.definitionFit: Something with real impact is said to work well, and that property of working is its potency.

clue.text: Reluctant to add a piece of poetry to article

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
a verse is a stanza or piece of poetry

explanation.surface: A writer is unwilling to tack a poem onto a newspaper story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece but is the grammatical article A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unwilling or opposed to something is a reluctant attitude.

clue.text: Beyond the allotted span for a breather?

definitions.text: Beyond the allotted span for a breather?

parts.words: Beyond the allotted span for a breather?
parts.note: a breather is anyone alive, and the allotted span is the biblical threescore years and ten; living past it is a lengthy existence

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase also describes milk or batteries that keep well, but here the 'breather' is a living creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Surviving past the normal human lifespan means enjoying great longevity.

clue.text: Turn-coat turned sailor?

indicators.note: turned tells us to read the word for a seaman backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A deserter who switched sides and went to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for a defector or traitor who abandons a cause.

clue.text: A Javanese tree found in an ashanti arboretum

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An Indonesian species is spotted in an African tree collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The antiar is the upas tree of Java, whose sap was used as arrow poison.

clue.text: Cardinal distinction

definitions.meaning: a cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church is addressed by this title

explanation.definitionFit: His Eminence is a cardinal's formal style, and the word also means prominence or renown.

clue.text: The point of many an old writer

definitions.text: The point of many an old writer

parts.words: The point of many an old writer
parts.note: an old writer here is a pen or quill, whose tip does the writing

explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' is the instrument, not the author.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal tip of a fountain or dip pen is where ink meets the page.

clue.text: Extremely uneven rum!

parts.note: very means extremely
an odd number is uneven, not divisible by two

explanation.surface: A remark that a drink of rum is decidedly lopsided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is the old British adjective meaning strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum in British slang means peculiar, and something highly peculiar is exceptionally strange.

clue.text: Let this free?

parts.note: put the word after let and the phrase means release without punishment

explanation.definitionFit: To let someone go unpunished is a common idiom built from let plus this adverb.

clue.text: Reproach for wound on her head?

definitions.meaning: a plait of hair coiled up on top of a woman's head

explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' is the past tense of wind, not an injury; split as UP BRAID it describes a coiled plait.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone sharply is to rebuke them, and a plait pinned up is a raised braid.

clue.text: Number the relatives curled in agony, though the dish was only a little one

definitions.text: the dish was only a little one

indicators.note: in places the number and the curled-up relatives inside the word for agony

parts.note: pain is agony

indicators.note: curled means the word for family is bent back on itself and read in reverse

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Family members writhe in pain, though the dish they fought over was tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: A pannikin is chiefly an Australian or old British word for a small tin mug or pan; 'Number the relatives' reads as an instruction to count, but supplies the inserted letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannikin is a small metal cup or pan, a little vessel for food or drink.

clue.text: A revolutionary cover for postbox

parts.note: red is the colour of revolutionaries, and a British pillar box is coated in it

explanation.walkthrough: British postboxes are painted bright red; 'revolutionary' also hints at the colour's political sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Coating of scarlet colour is applied to the pillar boxes of the Royal Mail.

clue.text: Strengthen one's position if entering two scores

indicators.note: entering means the small word goes inside the number

parts.note: a score is twenty, so two scores make forty

explanation.surface: A team boosts its standing after twice reaching twenty points, with a condition attached.
explanation.definitionFit: To fortify is to reinforce defences, strengthening a position.

clue.text: One of the media for whom the writing's on the wall

definitions.text: One of the media for whom the writing's on the wall

parts.words: One of the media for whom the writing's on the wall
parts.note: media here is the plural of medium, a means of expression; this one is words scrawled on walls

explanation.walkthrough: 'media' suggests the press; the singular form of the Italian plural is meant, a single wall scrawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A single scribbled inscription on a public wall is the singular of graffiti.

clue.text: The end of course

parts.note: the end of a racecourse is the line where the race is decided

explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but it is the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The last stretch or line of a race is where runners complete it.

clue.text: The woodlouse, for example, is round above shell

parts.note: O is round in shape
a pod is the shell of peas or beans

explanation.surface: A woodlouse curls into a ball on top of its hard casing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' puts IS + O over POD.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodlice belong to the order of crustaceans with similar legs throughout.

clue.text: Gave his agreement but wasn't fully awake

definitions.meaning: indicated assent with a movement of the head

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to something while half asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip of the head signals yes, and a drowsy person's head drops in the same way.

clue.text: Colours aren't secure so flee

definitions.meaning: dyes that are not fast spread in the wash

explanation.definitionFit: Dyes bleeding in the wash is said to happen when they are not fast; fleeing is going off at speed.

clue.text: Good works of relief do attract special notice

definitions.meaning: carving in relief has figures projecting from the background

explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' suggests charity, but it is sculpture in relief, whose figures project.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpted figures in relief project from their surface, and anything conspicuous projects from its surroundings.

clue.text: Such mental pictures when ether first

annotationWithheld.clue: Such mental pictures when ether first

clue.text: Penn was entertaining his followers and lots of pals

definitions.meaning: William Penn was a Quaker, and Quakers are the Society of Friends; he would be giving hospitality to them

explanation.walkthrough: William Penn, founder of Pennsylvania, was a Quaker, a member of the Religious Society of Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainer of Quakers receives guests from that Society, and a multitude of companions is the everyday phrase.
